instruction: Enable automatic screen lock on my computer.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent navigated Settings > Privacy > Screen and enabled the Automatic Screen Lock toggle (org.gnome.desktop.screensaver lock-enabled = true). Also changed blank screen delay from Never to 5 minutes.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can navigate GNOME Settings menus, find Privacy > Screen section, and toggle screen lock settings.
metadata.explanation: Task requires enabling the Automatic Screen Lock toggle in GNOME Settings > Privacy > Screen. Evaluator checks that org.gnome.desktop.screensaver lock-enabled is set to true via gsettings. Initial state has lock-enabled=false (setup step), so the initial state fails. Score is 1.0 if lock is enabled, 0.0 otherwise. [Fixed: renamed function MD5 suffixes from 8-char 'cde9b091' to correct 32-char hash '74e051f75a4f9998d114f6407d55ddd5' computed from 'a4d98375-215b-4a4d-aee9-3d4370fccc41|0']
fix_history: Fix 1: Renamed getter from 'get_screen_lock_state__cde9b091' to 'get_screen_lock_state__74e051f75a4f9998d114f6407d55ddd5' (correct 32-char MD5 of 'a4d98375-215b-4a4d-aee9-3d4370fccc41|0')
Fix 3: Updated evaluator.func and evaluator.result.type in task JSON to match new 32-char hash

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly reads 'org.gnome.desktop.screensaver lock-enabled' via gsettings, which is the precise GNOME setting controlling automatic screen lock.
Metric correctly checks 'true' in lock_str.lower(): gsettings output is literally 'true' or 'false', so this reliably returns 1.0 when enabled and 0.0 when not.
Setup sets lock-enabled=false, ensuring the initial state fails and providing proper negative control resistance.
The instruction 'Enable automatic screen lock' maps directly and completely to this single gsettings key; no additional requirements are missing.
Output is stripped of whitespace before comparison, handling edge cases in gsettings output.
